claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered ride (F9), for which the fare is driven by distance, so every extra kilometre billed is money the rider should not have paid.
GPS shows the trip ran 9.3 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, +5.4 km (+136%), and took 26.5 min against an 8 min estimate (F1, F3).
The track contains exactly two off-route segments: 14:10–14:13 adding 1.63 km and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.83 km (F4, F5), totalling 4.46 km of off-route excess.

The 14:10–14:13 segment (F4) is explained by the driver's own pre-trip request to go 'round by Cavenagh' (F10), which the rider accepted at 14:02 (F11); that acceptance was given before the segment started, so this segment is exempt.

The 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) is not covered by that consent: the rider's 14:02 message agreed only to the Cavenagh route and asked for a 7-Eleven stop (F11), and the driver unilaterally chose the Beach Road store (F13), which sits 1553 m off the optimal route.

The rider agreed to 'a stop', not to the route change; because the driver picked an off-route location on his own initiative, the extra distance on the 14:17–14:29 segment is not exempted by the rider's stop request (F5, F11, F13).

The stop ran 4 min 10 s at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2) and was billed $1.08 in waiting (F7); on a RydeTAXI the metered waiting unit is chargeable, so this $1.08 is not recoverable and the rider's case is confined to the mileage.
Refund on the non-exempt segment = 2.83 extra km × $1.41/km per-km rate (F6: $7.58 ÷ 5.4 km) = $3.9903, rounded to $3.99, which is the only mileage the driver should not have earned.

The driver's congestion defence does not fit the evidence: the Orchard Road band 1 record (F14) and the 13:52 accident 30 m from the optimal route (F17) cover only the earlier 14:10–14:13 segment, and nothing in the traffic facts justifies a 3.60 km loop out to Beach Road at 14:17–14:29 (F15, F16 show flow of 30–39 and 20–29 km/h on the other roads).
An unexempted off-route segment is enough to record a breach of the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route duty, with no percentage or kilometre threshold required (F5).

The driver has 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 already upheld (no-show) (F20); a further upheld route deviation in this case would make him 'repeated' and warrants an account review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The rider accepted the driver's Cavenagh proposal in writing at 14:02 (F11), so the driver will argue that consent extended to the whole reroute, and the 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) is merely the continuation of an agreed route.

The driver's statement (F13), backed by chat #1 (F10), gives a plausible 'reasonable cause' story for congestion, and there is a genuine band 1 record on Orchard Road plus an accident 30 m from the optimal route (F14, F17) — the rider must argue those cover only the earlier segment, not the Beach Road loop.

The rider did ask for a stop (F11) without naming a location and then never objected when the driver took the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F13); the driver will say the rider acquiesced, and only RD-3(b) defeats that argument.

The $4.50–$5.40 of mileage excess tied to the Cavenagh leg (F4: 1.63 km × $1.41 = $2.30) plus part of the 5.4 km billed excess (F6) is likely to be treated as exempt, so the rider cannot claim the full $7.58 and must accept a partial refund.
The waiting charge of $1.08 (F2, F7) is chargeable on a RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) and is a weakness if the rider argues for the full $6.61-style recovery.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.99 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
RydeTAXI is metered, so distance flows straight into the fare and any unexempted extra kilometre is money the rider should not have paid [F9][F6][RD-2]. The record gives two off-route segments: 14:10–14:13 adding 1.63 km [F4] and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.83 km [F5]; both parties now accept the first is exempt and dispute only the second [F4][F5][RD-1].

Segment F4 is exempt under the reasonable-cause branch: an accident was reported at 13:52 on the optimal route (30 m away, two lanes closed) and Orchard Road sat at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) across 14:00–14:10, covering the 14:10–14:13 window [F17][F14][F4][RD-4]. The trace confirms the incident qualifies, so no refund attaches to that 1.63 km [F4][RD-4][RD-2].

Segment F5 is not exempt. The driver's pre-departure consent request named only "go round by Cavenagh," and the rider's 14:02 "Sure" agreed to that named corridor [F10][F11]. Consent is measured by what the driver actually named before leaving; a 3.60 km loop out to Beach Road running up to 1553 m off the optimal route plainly goes somewhere other than the named Cavenagh corridor, so RD-5 does not reach this segment [F5][F10][F11][F13][RD-5]. claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered ride (F9), for which the fare is driven by distance, so every extra kilometre billed is money the rider should not have paid.
GPS shows the trip ran 9.3 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, +5.4 km (+136%), and took 26.5 min against an 8 min estimate (F1, F3).
The track contains exactly two off-route segments: 14:10–14:13 adding 1.63 km and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.83 km (F4, F5), totalling 4.46 km of off-route excess.

The 14:10–14:13 segment (F4) is explained by the driver's own pre-trip request to go 'round by Cavenagh' (F10), which the rider accepted at 14:02 (F11); that acceptance was given before the segment started, so this segment is exempt.

The 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) is not covered by that consent: the rider's 14:02 message agreed only to the Cavenagh route and asked for a 7-Eleven stop (F11), and the driver unilaterally chose the Beach Road store (F13), which sits 1553 m off the optimal route.

The rider agreed to 'a stop', not to the route change; because the driver picked an off-route location on his own initiative, the extra distance on the 14:17–14:29 segment is not exempted by the rider's stop request (F5, F11, F13).

The stop ran 4 min 10 s at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2) and was billed $1.08 in waiting (F7); on a RydeTAXI the metered waiting unit is chargeable, so this $1.08 is not recoverable and the rider's case is confined to the mileage.
Refund on the non-exempt segment = 2.83 extra km × $1.41/km per-km rate (F6: $7.58 ÷ 5.4 km) = $3.9903, rounded to $3.99, which is the only mileage the driver should not have earned.

The driver's congestion defence does not fit the evidence: the Orchard Road band 1 record (F14) and the 13:52 accident 30 m from the optimal route (F17) cover only the earlier 14:10–14:13 segment, and nothing in the traffic facts justifies a 3.60 km loop out to Beach Road at 14:17–14:29 (F15, F16 show flow of 30–39 and 20–29 km/h on the other roads).
An unexempted off-route segment is enough to record a breach of the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route duty, with no percentage or kilometre threshold required (F5).

The driver has 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 already upheld (no-show) (F20); a further upheld route deviation in this case would make him 'repeated' and warrants an account review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The rider accepted the driver's Cavenagh proposal in writing at 14:02 (F11), so the driver will argue that consent extended to the whole reroute, and the 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) is merely the continuation of an agreed route.

The driver's statement (F13), backed by chat #1 (F10), gives a plausible 'reasonable cause' story for congestion, and there is a genuine band 1 record on Orchard Road plus an accident 30 m from the optimal route (F14, F17) — the rider must argue those cover only the earlier segment, not the Beach Road loop.

The rider did ask for a stop (F11) without naming a location and then never objected when the driver took the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F13); the driver will say the rider acquiesced, and only RD-3(b) defeats that argument.

The $4.50–$5.40 of mileage excess tied to the Cavenagh leg (F4: 1.63 km × $1.41 = $2.30) plus part of the 5.4 km billed excess (F6) is likely to be treated as exempt, so the rider cannot claim the full $7.58 and must accept a partial refund.
